subdomain: 1.4 Design multi-agent systems and orchestration strategies

en.question: A lead agent revises a study from plan A to plan B while asynchronous workers are still running. A late worker returns a valid result for plan A after several plan B results. The final report must use one approved plan and data snapshot. How should the orchestrator prevent a mixed report?

options.text: Accept results in arrival order and let the most recently returned findings replace earlier findings on the same topic.
options.note: Arrival order reflects execution timing, not semantic compatibility. A late result can belong to the superseded plan and overwrite current evidence.

options.text: Broadcast the new plan once and assume every result received after that message was produced under the revised instructions.
options.note: In-flight workers may already have used the old plan or snapshot. A notification alone does not establish which version a returned artifact represents.

options.text: Combine both sets of findings and ask a synthesis model to prefer whichever passages appear more detailed and internally consistent.
options.note: Detail and internal consistency do not establish that evidence belongs to the approved plan. Content-based preference cannot enforce a version boundary.

options.text: Identify every assignment and result by plan and data snapshot, reconciling incompatible versions before accepting evidence into synthesis.
options.note: Explicit identities let the coordinator distinguish stale work from current work despite asynchronous arrival. Reconciliation or rerunning is required before incompatible evidence enters the approved report.

references.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
